required_evidence: Resolve whether vanishing reduced records in a finite-length complex of complex Hilbert spaces implies the proposed bounded chain contraction.
A legal counterexample must verify the reduced record vanishes at every degree, including endpoints, and must use complex Hilbert spaces as stated.
Any positive bounded-solver claim must establish its actual lower bound, surjectivity, or a sufficient closed-range argument.
critical_errors: Interpret finite length as finite-dimensional layers.
Drop closure bars from boundary spaces without proof.
Infer a spectral gap, surjectivity, or a bounded inverse from a zero kernel.
Promote a regularized approximation to an exact bounded contraction, or strong convergence to operator-norm convergence.
Present a correctly stated theorem under added closed-range assumptions as a proof of the original universal target.
completion_policy: A legal counterexample disproving the universal target completes the main task. Do not require the closed-range classification, regularization, or the author example. Explicit closed-range conditional constructions are valid contributions; they are not silently treated as original hypotheses.
open_task_policy: Accept independently verified alternative constructions, counterexamples and unexpected results. Explicit conditional results are valid contributions; silently promoting their scope is not. Honest incompleteness is distinct from an invalid proof.
